group.passage: Taiwanese opera began in Yilan more than a hundred years ago and is one of the few art forms born in Taiwan. Below, an actress talks about her life on stage, and a high school student describes the first show he watched in a theater.

passage_parts.label: A
passage_parts.title: Playing a Hero
passage_parts.text: As a child, I spent many evenings with my grandmother in front of our local temple. During temple festivals, a stage was set up outside, and we sat on plastic stools for hours to watch Taiwanese opera. When I joined a group of actors at sixteen, my teacher asked me to play young male heroes. In Taiwanese opera, these roles are often played by women, and many fans love these actresses. Playing a man on stage was hard. I had to lower my voice, walk with big steps, and stand with my chest out. Outdoor shows are still my favorite. We often make up some lines on the spot, and the crowd shouts back at us, so no two shows are the same. Today, younger actors are bringing in new ideas, such as rock music and modern costumes, but the old songs remain at the heart of every show.

passage_parts.label: B
passage_parts.title: My First Taiwanese Opera
passage_parts.text: I used to think Taiwanese opera was only for grandparents. Most of the people I had noticed at shows near my home had white hair. Last weekend, though, my aunt took me to a theater in Taipei, and I was surprised. The stage was full of color, the drums were exciting, and the fights looked like a dance. Words on a screen beside the stage helped me follow the story, since my Taiwanese is not very good. The best part was the hero. He was brave, funny, and kind, and he was played by a woman! I did not realize it until my aunt told me after the show. Now I want to go to an outdoor show at a temple, where, my aunt says, the actors joke with the crowd. I am going to bring my friends.

translation_zh.text:
歌仔戲一百多年前起源於宜蘭，是少數在臺灣誕生的藝術形式之一。以下是一位女演員談她的舞臺生涯，以及一位高中生描述他第一次在劇院看的演出。
A 扮演英雄：小時候，我有很多個晚上都和祖母待在我們當地的廟前。廟會期間，外面會搭起戲臺，我們坐在塑膠凳子上，一看就是好幾個小時的歌仔戲。我十六歲加入戲班時，老師要我演年輕的男主角。在歌仔戲裡，這些角色常由女性扮演，許多戲迷也很喜愛這些女演員。在臺上扮演男人很難。我得壓低聲音、大步走路、挺起胸膛站著。戶外演出到現在還是我的最愛。我們常常當場編一些臺詞，觀眾也會大聲回應我們，所以沒有兩場演出是一樣的。現在，年輕的演員帶進了新點子，例如搖滾樂和現代風格的戲服，但老曲調仍是每場演出的核心。
B 我的第一場歌仔戲：我以前以為歌仔戲只是爺爺奶奶在看的。我在家附近的演出看到的觀眾，大多數都是白頭髮。不過上個週末，阿姨帶我去臺北的一間劇院，我很驚訝。舞臺色彩繽紛，鼓聲讓人興奮，打鬥場面看起來就像一支舞。舞臺旁螢幕上的字幕幫我跟上劇情，因為我的臺語不太好。最精彩的是男主角。他勇敢、風趣又善良，而他是由一位女性扮演的！直到演出結束阿姨告訴我，我才發現。現在我想去看廟口的戶外演出，阿姨說在那裡演員會和觀眾說笑。我打算帶朋友一起去。

problems: 引言 “… is one of the few art forms born in Taiwan.” 把事實單 f2 的 one of the few Han art forms 簡化成 one of the few art forms，略為誇大（臺灣原住民族的許多藝術也誕生於臺灣）；常見說法是「臺灣土生土長的戲曲劇種」。不影響任何一題作答（四題都不考這句）。建議人工審核確認，下一版改成 one of the few kinds of theater born in Taiwan 之類的說法。
